blocks.html: Picture Camille, a young executive in Ortigas Center heading to Opus in Bridgetowne for a business lunch. Ordinarily, she would take her car, navigate midday traffic, and look for parking before making her way to the restaurant. With the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority’s (MMDA) newly launched Love Bus service, she can simply walk to the pickup point at Robinsons Galleria and catch a ride to Bridgetowne, leaving the driving to someone else. Best of all, it’s free!

To those who live or work near the Love Bus route, the service offers a welcome reason to leave the car at home when heading to the office, meeting friends for lunch, or spending an afternoon at the mall. Regularly scheduled departures bring greater predictability and efficiency to everyday travel, helping passengers plan their trips without having to budget for fuel, fares for ride-hailing services, or worry about parking.

With its donation of buses in support of the MMDA initiative, Robinsons Land Corporation (RLC), is helping bring back the iconic bus service remembered by an earlier generation of commuters. Today, that familiar name returns with a focus on more sustainable mobility: electric buses that produce zero tailpipe emissions, giving passengers a cleaner transport option for everyday trips.

Six buses, each accommodating 36 passengers, operate daily from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., providing free rides along a route connecting Robinsons Galleria, Ortigas Avenue, C5, Bridgetowne, as well as other key developments.

“Hop in, Hop Out” captures the service’s simple, easygoing appeal. Whether heading to a meeting or returning from the mall with full shopping bags, passengers can enjoy a comfortable ride in the new buses, with clean, spacious interiors and air-conditioning offering a refreshing escape from the heat outside.

The initiative brings MMDA, local governments, and private sector partners closer together to serve communities along the route, including developments beyond RLC’s own properties. This cooperation gives residents, workers, and visitors a shared transport option for their everyday journeys.
For Camille and many other typical commuters, it allows a welcome break from being behind the wheel and one less thing to organize in an already busy day. What’s not to love?
